subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: helping a friend who is being targeted [Action]
passage: Rafiq noticed it during computer period: a classmate, Tanya, being mocked in the group chat, with joke after joke about a photo of her. Nobody stopped. Rafiq didn't add a laugh and didn't forward anything. Instead, Rafiq took screenshots of the messages, the names and the times. At the break Rafiq sent Tanya a private message: “I saw. I'm sorry. It's not okay. Do you want company?” Tanya replied after a minute: “Yes.” They met at the library. “Shall we tell Dhruv Sir together?” Rafiq asked. Tanya nodded, though her hands shook. Dhruv Sir listened, thanked them both for bringing the screenshots, and said he'd pass it to the safety lead that day and keep her name out of it.

qa.q: What did Rafiq do with the messages?
qa.a: Took screenshots of the messages, names and times.

qa.q: How might Tanya have felt when Rafiq's private message arrived?
qa.a: Relieved that someone cared, though still embarrassed and shaky about what had happened.

qa.q: What else could Rafiq do to support Tanya, and why?
qa.a: Keep checking in and sit with Tanya at lunch, since a friend nearby can make going to school easier.

qa.q: How does the situation look to Dhruv Sir?
qa.a: Dhruv Sir sees two students bringing proof and asking for help, so he can act the same day without exposing Tanya.

grounding: A teen who sees a classmate mocked in a group chat does not join in, checks on her privately, saves the messages and goes to a teacher together.

subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: helping a friend who is being targeted [Action]
passage:
Dear Tarun Sir,
I'm writing about something happening in our class chat group. Since Monday, some people have been posting mocking comments and edited pictures about Sabeena, mostly about her weight and her voice. I haven't added anything or passed any of it on.
On Tuesday I messaged Sabeena privately to ask if she was okay. She said she hadn't eaten lunch in two days because she didn't want to sit in the canteen. I have saved screenshots of the messages, with names and times, in a folder on my phone.
Sabeena is scared to come to you alone, but she has agreed to come with me. Could we both meet you tomorrow before assembly?
Gurleen, 9B

Reply, 6:40 pm, same day:
Gurleen, thank you. You did exactly the right thing. I have called Sabeena's parents this evening. Please both come to the staffroom at 7:45 tomorrow and bring the screenshots.
T. Singh

qa.q: When does Tarun Sir ask them to come?
qa.a: At 7:45 tomorrow, to the staffroom, with the screenshots.

qa.q: What might Gurleen be worried about in writing the email?
qa.a: Gurleen is worried about Sabeena skipping lunch and being scared, and wants help to come quickly.

qa.q: What else could Gurleen do in the class group itself?
qa.a: Stay out of it and not react, and perhaps quietly ask a few classmates not to forward anything.

qa.q: How might Sabeena feel about going to the teacher with Gurleen?
qa.a: Sabeena may still feel scared, but less alone, since a classmate stands beside her and has already gathered proof.

grounding: Shows a teen who does not join or forward mockery of a classmate, checks on her privately, saves the messages and brings her to a teacher together.

subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: helping a friend who is being targeted [Action]
passage:
You asked what I'd do if it happened in our group, Indu. It already did, last month, so I'll just tell you. I'm Vidya, and I was scared the whole time, just so you know.
Someone posted a photo of Mariam asleep on the bus with a cruel caption, and then everyone added stickers. I felt sick. I didn't add anything, and I didn't forward it, even when someone asked, “Did you see?”
That evening I messaged Mariam alone: “I saw. Are you okay?” She said she was fine. Ten minutes later: “Not really.”
I took screenshots of the whole thread, names and times showing, and showed Amma before bed. She messaged Mehta Ma'am right then. Next morning I told Mariam, “Let's go to Ma'am together. You don't have to talk, I'll start.” She came. Ma'am read everything, called Mariam's mother from the staffroom, and by lunch the posts were gone.
Mariam sits with me at lunch now.

qa.q: What did Mariam reply ten minutes later?
How was Vidya feeling while all this happened?
qa.a: Vidya felt scared the whole time and sick at the stickers, but still acted.

qa.q: What else could Vidya have done when someone asked "Did you see?"
qa.a: Simply not respond, or say privately that it isn't funny, staying out of the pile-on while adults handled it.

qa.q: What was it like for Mariam to get a message from Vidya alone?
qa.a: It let Mariam admit to not being fine and gave her company going to the teacher, which made asking for help possible.

grounding: Shows a teen who doesn't join or forward mockery of a classmate, checks on her privately, saves the messages and goes with her to a teacher.
